questions.question: Nebraska's speed law requires you to drive:

options.text: Five miles per hour above the posted speed limit.
At a speed that is reasonable and safe for current conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a speed that is reasonable and safe for current conditions.
questions.explanation: Nebraska's speed law requires you to drive at a speed that is reasonable and safe for current conditions, but not faster than the posted speed limit. Slow down whenever conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: If you change your name or address, Nebraska law requires you to apply for a new operator's license within:
questions.correctAnswerText: 60 days.
questions.explanation: If your name changes, go to a Driver Licensing Office. If your address changes, go to a Driver Licensing Office or apply online. You must do this within 60 days of the change.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with no traffic control signs or signals, a driver should:

options.text: Keep your speed and go through.
Stop at the intersection, look in all directions, and then go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, yield to vehicles coming from your right. Always be ready to yield to avoid a crash. Do this by easing off the gas, being ready to brake, and looking left, right, and left again.

questions.question: The minimum legal speed on interstate highways is:
questions.correctAnswerText: 40 mph.
questions.explanation: The minimum speed limit on Nebraska interstate highways is 40 miles per hour. Only drive slower than this if conditions require it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down and let trains pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and let trains pass.
questions.explanation: A round sign means a railroad crossing is ahead. The sign is placed a few hundred feet before the tracks. It tells drivers to slow down, listen, look, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: When a fire truck is responding to an emergency, no vehicle may follow it closer than:
questions.correctAnswerText: 500 feet.
questions.explanation: You must stay at least 500 feet behind a fire truck responding to an emergency. Do not park within one block of where a fire truck has stopped for an emergency.

questions.question: When leaving an alley or driveway to enter the street, drivers should:

options.text: Stop only if people are on the sidewalk.
Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
Expect people on the sidewalk to get out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before driving onto the sidewalk.
questions.explanation: When leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot, you must stop before driving onto the sidewalk. Pedestrians and other traffic have the right-of-way.

questions.question: Which is the safest way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep the same speed through the whole curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve and gradually speed up as you exit. Speeding up as you enter a curve makes your vehicle harder to control.

questions.question: It is legal to drive faster than the speed limit when passing another vehicle.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You can never drive faster than the posted speed limit, even when passing another vehicle.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, you should:

options.text: Give a short, loud horn blast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give a short, loud horn blast.
questions.explanation: If there is danger, use a short, loud horn blast. Do this when a child or any person is about to step into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.
questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control traffic. They are white with black markings. Drivers must always obey them.

questions.question: You are driving on a busy street and your vehicle's accelerator gets stuck open. You should:

options.text: Turn off your ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If the accelerator sticks, the engine will keep the car moving even when you lift your foot off the gas. Turn off the ignition carefully. Move the key only enough to stop the engine without locking the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and move to a safe area.

questions.question: Which of the following directs drivers into the proper lanes for turning on some highways?

options.text: White lines on the side of the road
White arrows in the middle of the lanes

questions.correctAnswerText: White arrows in the middle of the lanes
questions.explanation: White arrows show drivers which lanes to use. They indicate whether you should go straight or turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It means you cannot drive in this direction.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the curb.
Turn them slightly to the right.
Turn them sharply away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. This keeps your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail.

questions.question: At a four-way stop, the driver on the right should insist on having the right-of-way.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Never demand your right-of-way. Always give up your right-of-way if it prevents an accident.

questions.question: When stopping on snow or ice with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), you should:

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
Stay off the brakes and let the car drift to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal firmly and hold it when stopping on snow or ice in a car with ABS. The ABS will pump the brakes faster than you can.

questions.question: What do broken yellow lines mean on streets and highways?

options.text: They separate lanes moving in the same direction.
They separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: They separate lanes moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines mean passing is allowed when it is safe.

questions.question: At a stop sign, after you stop, what should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgating cars.
Move when the car ahead moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because cars from the left are closer to you. Then look right. Then look left again to catch any cars you missed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this intersection. It is unsafe and against the law.

questions.question: You can never turn left at a red light.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: You may turn left at a red light if there is no sign prohibiting it AND you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street. This is the only situation where a left turn on red is allowed.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, what must you do?

options.text: Give the right-of-way to any traffic that is close enough to cause a collision.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and keep going without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to any traffic that is close enough to cause a collision.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any crossing or merging traffic that is close enough to cause a collision.

questions.question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?

options.text: Slow down before you enter the exit ramp.
Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
Keep your speed the same once you are on the exit ramp.
Pass slower cars on the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down after you move onto the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down until after you move onto the exit ramp.

questions.question: When can you legally turn left at a red light after stopping?

options.text: When you are on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.
When you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
When you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street.
questions.explanation: After a complete stop, you can turn left at a red light only when you are on a one-way street and turning onto another one-way street. Make sure there are no signs that prohibit this turn.

questions.question: When you plan to pass another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Do not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not assume the other driver will make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even if you signal, do not assume the space you want is free or that other drivers will give you the right-of-way.
